name: insolvia-workspace
//: Root of the Insolvia npm workspace. NOT a shippable package — it declares
the members and pins the shared toolchain, mirroring what pubspec.yaml does
for the Dart workspace it is replacing.
The member list is EXPLICIT and must stay that way. `packages/*` would
swallow packages/insolvia_design_system_react, which publishes to GitHub
Packages and is consumed by the marketing site BY VERSION, never by path.
Making it a workspace member would silently symlink marketing to the local
source, so a broken package would pass CI and only fail after publishing —
the exact trap the root pubspec.yaml documents for the Flutter design
system. apps/insolvia_marketing is out for the same reason: it resolves
CAUTION — Node resolution walks UP the tree, which pub never did. A missing
can now resolve from this root's node_modules and pass CI, then fail in a
clean install. Both keep their own package-lock.json and their own CI job
installs from it, which is what catches this — do not consolidate them here.

//tokens: Run with plain `node`, no loader and no build step: Node >=24 strips
TypeScript types natively, so the generator keeps the dependency-free
property its Dart predecessor was written to defend. Type-stripping
cannot execute `enum`, `namespace`, or parameter properties — the
//lint: Members are named explicitly rather than globbed, matching the
changed-paths convention in design-system-pr.yml. A bare `eslint .` would
descend into the marketing site and the React design system, which have
their own configs, their own lockfiles, and their own required checks.
A new member adds its line here.
//ci: The npm half of the gate only. While the Dart half still exists,
`melos run ci` remains the other half; PR 3 deletes it and leaves this.
scripts.ci: npm run tokens:check && npm run format && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test

//devDependencies: ESLint/Prettier versions match apps/insolvia_marketing deliberately — the
app added in PR 3 is told to match marketing's lint setup, so a second
ESLint major in the repo would be a trap, not a choice.
TypeScript is 5.9 rather than the 7.x line: `erasableSyntaxOnly` (5.8+) is
the feature this workspace depends on, and adopting a rewritten compiler in
the middle of a toolchain migration would confound any failure.
